title: Alternating media CTA
description: A stacked pair or list of two-column CTA rows where text cards and images alternate left/right.

aliases.purpose: Legacy names from existing projects. Agents use these only to find and map old implementations; new code must use the canonical naming fields.

projects.name: edge
projects.note: Edge names this visual block detailing-consultation and stores CMS data under detailingConsultation:detailingConsultation.

projects.name: hvoya-cms-preview
projects.note: Hvoya uses the related comfort-details/informations implementation for alternating media/text rows.

agent.usage: Use this block when the target section is a list of two-column CTA rows with a text card, primary CTA, and image, where row direction alternates on desktop and stacks text before image on mobile.
transferSteps: Copy section-alternating-media-cta.blade.php as the target section view unless the project has an explicit naming map.
Ensure required foundation styles and the button partial exist before adding block-specific SCSS.
Add an alternatingMediaCta:alternatingMediaCta collection fixture or map an existing legacy key through the target CMS layer.
Copy block image assets or map CMS image fields to project-owned assets.
Override local --alternating-media-cta-* tokens when the target project needs different spacing or geometry.
Do not duplicate container or button foundation styles inside the block SCSS.
acceptance: Rendered section has the canonical .alternating-media-cta class.
Rendered section wraps the list in .container.alternating-media-cta__container without block-specific .container overrides.
Desktop rendering alternates the second row with .alternating-media-cta__item--reverse.
Mobile rendering stacks content before media for every item.
Block-specific spacing and geometry are exposed through local --alternating-media-cta-* tokens.
Block-specific SCSS does not target or override .section-title, .section-text, .container, or .button.
CTA buttons render through the foundation button partial/classes only, without a local block-specific button class.
Title, text, images, and CTA can be changed through CMS data.
